narrative.h2: Reels rewards visual polish over raw novelty

sections.heading: Why Reels is its own conversation
sections.body: Instagram's audience skews older and more brand-trained than TikTok's. Reels users will tolerate a slower opening, but they're less forgiving of low-production-value footage — the platform is still aspirational by default. The 90-second ceiling means you have more room for a verse and a chorus, and the native music library means you can upload your track as a Reels audio and let other creators use it, which is the actual distribution play for musicians on this platform.

sections.heading: Conventions that win on Reels
sections.body: Color-graded, deliberate composition, lyric overlays in clean sans-serif type, transitions that match the beat without screaming about it. The Reels aesthetic borrows more from fashion film than from TikTok's chaos — think Daniel Caesar's videos, Steve Lacy's visual rollouts, the way FKA Twigs treats every frame as a still. Vertical 9:16, hook by the 5-second mark, but the first 5 seconds can earn that hook with a build.

sections.heading: Tunee's Reels export and the audio play
sections.body: The Reels preset outputs 9:16 at 1080p, 90 seconds max, with the audio track exported separately as an MP3 you can upload as a Reels Audio. That's the multiplier — your video gets played once, your audio gets used by 50 other creators who tag back. Tunee also generates a 30-second 'tease' cut alongside the full Reel for cross-posting as a Story, so one generation seeds three distribution surfaces.
